principles: Prefer evidence over reimplementation when the implementation already exists and passes selfcheck
Keep runner semantics and paper wording aligned to the same spend-matched definition
Avoid introducing churn in a verified recovery-runner path
drivers: Proofbound worktree is currently code-clean for the target files
The selfcheck already proves the accounting and budget helpers
The companion paper appendix/protocol had stale call-count wording that needed sync

options.name: A: Verify-and-sync
pros: Keeps the story focused on evidence and paper wording alignment
Minimizes risk of drift or accidental behavior changes
cons: Does not produce a new proofbound code diff
Requires a separate paper sync step to keep the manuscript consistent

options.name: B: Re-edit runner logic
pros: Creates a visible proofbound code change
Can force the story to look implementation-heavy
cons: Duplicates logic that is already correct
Risks regressing a verified path or introducing mismatched semantics
Adds churn without improving the measured behavior

rationale: The worktree already contains the required accounting and spend-matching behavior, and the no-LLM selfcheck passes. Re-editing the runner would be redundant and risky, so the better completion path is to verify the existing implementation and sync the paper protocol/manuscript wording to match it.

preMortem.scenario: Paper wording stays stale after proofbound verification
preMortem.trigger: Only the runner is validated and the manuscript/protocol appendix remains on the old call-count phrasing
preMortem.consequence: A future reader can reintroduce the wrong compute-control story
preMortem.mitigation: Patch experiment-protocol.md and the appendix in paper/main.tex to use the spend-matched wording

preMortem.scenario: Story is marked done without an evidence artifact
preMortem.trigger: We rely only on the code selfcheck and skip writing a summary note
preMortem.consequence: The paper repo loses the audit trail that this accounting change was verified
preMortem.mitigation: Add a short paper/evidence note summarizing the selfcheck and the semantic sync

preMortem.scenario: A redundant code edit sneaks in and changes semantics
preMortem.trigger: Trying to make the story look more active than it is
preMortem.consequence: The verified runner path could drift from the established selfcheck
preMortem.mitigation: Do not touch the proofbound recovery-runner logic unless a failing check appears
